## Dropship for SteamOS 0.1.3

The release that ends the *Dropship for SteamOS is not responding* dialog on the way out of a
session — the one that showed up when you shut the Deck down after playing a game with Dropship
open. Nothing about the server blocking changed.

### Fixed in this release

- **The window could stop responding, permanently, when a game went fullscreen over it.** A
  compositor does not have to keep answering a window it is not showing, and KWin does not: it
  holds the buffers it has already taken from a covered window. If Dropship was mid-frame at the
  moment it got covered — likely, since it keeps its status fresh every couple of seconds — that
  frame waited for a release that never came. The wait is inside the graphics driver, so the app
  stopped running entirely: it could not answer the desktop's ping when the session started
  shutting down, and minutes later you were asked whether to wait for it. It never came back, even
  once the window was visible again. Dropship now notices when it has not drawn for twenty seconds,
  which is three orders of magnitude longer than a frame can honestly take, and closes itself
  rather than hanging. A window that cannot draw is of no use to anyone; being gone is what keeps
  the dialog from appearing.

  This is a trade you should know about: if the window ever does wedge, it closes itself instead of
  sitting there frozen. There is no partial state — either the fix works or you lose a window you
  could not have used anyway.

Nothing else changed. If you never played a game with Dropship open before shutting down, this
release does nothing you can see.

### Verified on a real Steam Deck

- The stall itself, reproduced on demand: with the app hosted by a throwaway compositor, stopping
  that compositor for good leaves the installed 0.1.2 still wedged after 45 seconds. The fixed
  build leaves 22 seconds later, having written *"The window has not been drawn for 20s, which
  means the display has stopped answering it; leaving rather than hanging."*
- The two cases that must **not** trigger it: a healthy window left alone for 60 seconds is still
  running, and a stall that ends by itself (compositor stopped for 8 seconds, then resumed) is
  survived rather than turned into an exit.
- The binary tested on the Deck was verified by md5 against the CI artifact, not by name or date.
- Unchanged from 0.1.2: the nftables/cgroup-v2 blocking mechanism; the manual Apply and Disable
  path; the installer, launcher entry and uninstall round trip; the watcher service applying blocks
  on launch and removing them on exit.

### Not yet verified

The whole path in one go on real hardware: launch a real game over the window, then shut the Deck
down. The stall and the response to it are both proven separately, and the recording that
diagnosed this (per-thread CPU counters, sampled once a second) is what the 20-second number comes
from — but nobody has yet installed this build and played a game before powering off. If the dialog
still appears there, the message above will be in the journal with a timestamp, and that is the
next thing to look at.

Also unchanged from 0.1.2: a real Overwatch launch driving the automatic path end to end.

### Install

```sh
tar -xzf dropship-steamos-0.1.3-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd dropship-steamos-0.1.3
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
sudo ./install.sh
```

That installs the privileged helper, the watcher service and a **Dropship for SteamOS** entry in
the application launcher. Open it, choose your regions, and switch on **Block while Overwatch
runs**. Remove everything again with `sudo ./install.sh --uninstall`.

If you already have an earlier version installed, running the same commands upgrades it in place;
there is no separate upgrade step, and your region selection is left alone.

Requires x86_64 SteamOS. Built on Ubuntu 24.04, which is older than the Deck's glibc — so nothing
newer than what the Deck already has is required. The binaries are dynamically linked against
glibc, so they are not portable to musl distributions.
